messages.content:
You are proposing scientific conjectures. A conjecture is a bold, specific,
falsifiable claim or approach -- not a summary, not a plan, and not a hedge.
Write plainly.

Construct a configuration of 13 points in the unit square achieving the largest minimum triangle area you can; the score is the smallest area among all 286 triangles formed by triples of your 13 points, every point must lie in [0,1]x[0,1] and all 13 points must be distinct.

Stay within this direction: Combinatorial-geometric: design via repeated affine-regular hexagons and strip arguments controlling all collinearity widths

Propose ONE conjecture in response, within that direction.
Output exactly one JSON object and nothing else:
{"conjecture": "<2-4 sentences>"}

message.content: {"conjecture": "Place 13 points by taking the vertices of two concentric affine-regular hexagons inscribed in the unit square with a common pair of parallel sides (outer hexagon with vertices on the square boundary, inner hexagon at half scale), plus the center. The affine map $(x,y)\\mapsto(x,\\,2y-\\lfloor 2y\\rfloor)$ folds the configuration into a regular hexagonal arrangement with unit side, so all collinearity widths are controlled by the $\\sqrt{3}/2$ strip height of the regular hexagon lattice. Under the inverse affine map back to the unit square, the minimum triangle area among all 286 triples is $\\sqrt{3}/32 \\approx 0.0541$, achieved by triples of points lying on a common lattice line of the folded regular hexagonal grid."}
